item.research_question: Is polymorphism still possible in entropy-stabilized high-entropy alloys (HEAs) that are generally believed to possess extremely high structural stability and maintain a single-phase structure?
item.processing_route: Synthesized via gas-atomization (melt injected into high purity Ar at 4 MPa pressure); subjected to hydrostatic compression up to ~41 GPa using a diamond anvil cell (DAC) with helium as pressure-transmitting medium; subsequently heated using resistive heating (up to 723 K) or double-sided Nd:YLF laser heating (up to ~1,400 K) at various pressures (6, 14, 26 GPa).
item.test_conditions: Room temperature compression up to ~41 GPa; heating at ambient pressure up to 723 K; heating at 6, 14, and 26 GPa up to ~1,400 K; in situ synchrotron radiation X-ray diffraction (XRD) monitoring.
key_findings: The fcc-to-hcp polymorphic transition starts at approximately 22 GPa and almost completes at approximately 41 GPa.
The phase transition is irreversible; the hcp phase is retained when pressure is released to ambient conditions.
The hcp phase remains stable up to 633 K at ambient pressure before transforming back to fcc.
At 26 GPa, the critical temperature for the hcp-to-fcc transition is approximately 1,400 K.
The isothermal bulk modulus (B0) is 153.9±3.0 GPa for the fcc phase and 150.2±4.6 GPa for the hcp phase.
The c/a ratio of the hcp phase remained almost constant at 1.62±0.01 during compression and decompression.
The transition is sluggish, with fcc and hcp phases coexisting over a wide pressure range of ~22 to ~41 GPa.
Decompression from different maximum pressures yields fcc/hcp composites with tunable fractions.
item.mechanism: The transition occurs because the hcp structure is thermodynamically more favorable at lower temperatures and high pressures, while the fcc phase is stable at higher temperatures and lower pressures; the transition is kinetically hindered by high energy barriers and low stacking fault energy (~20 mJ m−2), requiring high pressure to overcome these barriers to form the hcp phase.
item.limitations: The transition is sluggish and irreversible, making it difficult to determine the real equilibrium phase boundary (Clapeyron coexistence curve) experimentally; grain size was not small enough for statistically reliable Rietveld refinement of volume fractions; overshooting often exists due to high energy barriers.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that this behavior could be general in various HEAs and propose new avenues for tailoring HEA properties via polymorphic transition-induced HEA composites, particularly at cryogenic temperatures where transition pressure could be largely decreased.
quotes: The transition is irreversible, and our in situ high-temperature synchrotron radiation X-ray diffraction experiments at different pressures of the retained hcp high-entropy alloy reveal that the fcc phase is a stable polymorph at high temperatures, while the hcp structure is more thermodynamically favourable at lower temperatures.

The transition was sluggish, the fcc and new phase coexisted over large pressure range. At the maximum pressure of ∼41 GPa, the diffraction reflections mainly corresponded to the new phase while only minute residual fcc phase remained.

Our findings indicate that this fcc HEA is a thermodynamically metastable polymorph obtained by kinetic constraints and the thermodynamically favourable hcp structure is relatively difficult to attain.
